quests.instruction: Here are three sentences about Dara's day. Which one tells how Dara FEELS?
quests.correctAnswer: Dara feels worried about the exam 😟
options: Dara's lunch box is on the table 🍱
Dara thinks the exam will be long 📝
Dara feels worried about the exam 😟
quests.hint: A feeling names what someone experiences inside. Which sentence has one?
quests.explanation: A feeling is what we experience inside, like worry. A thought is what we think about something, and a fact like a lunch box on a table is neither.
quests.funFact: A story has parts: what happened, what we think, what we feel, and what we do.

quests.instruction: Tomás is teased in the corridor. He feels angry and thinks, 'That is not fair!' Then he walks away and tells a teacher. Which of these is an ACTION?
quests.correctAnswer: He walks away and tells a teacher 🚶
options: He walks away and tells a teacher 🚶
He thinks, 'That is not fair!' 💭
His face feels hot 🔥
quests.hint: An action is something a person does that others can see.
quests.explanation: Walking away and telling a teacher is something Tomás does, so it is an action. A hot face is a body feeling and 'That is not fair!' is a thought.
quests.funFact: We can choose our actions even when our feelings are strong.

quests.instruction: Which sentence tells ONLY what happened, without a thought or a feeling?
quests.correctAnswer: The bell rang and the class lined up 🔔
options: The bell rang and the class lined up 🔔
Ravi felt rushed and tense 😬
Ravi thought the line was too long 💭
quests.hint: Look for the sentence with no opinion and no emotion words.
quests.explanation: 'The bell rang and the class lined up' states an event. The others describe how Ravi felt and what he thought.
quests.funFact: Separating what happened from how we feel about it helps us explain things clearly.

quests.instruction: Aanya thinks, 'Everyone will laugh if I forget my lines.' Which feeling is most likely to go with that thought?
quests.correctAnswer: Nervous 😬
options: Nervous 😬
Proud 😌
Bored 😑
quests.hint: Think about what kind of thought predicts something going wrong.
quests.explanation: A thought about something going wrong in front of others often goes with nervousness. Thoughts can start feelings.
quests.funFact: Noticing a thought can help you understand why a feeling showed up.

quests.instruction: Felix is very angry because his brother broke his toy. Which choice describes an ACTION, not a feeling?
quests.correctAnswer: Felix tells his brother, 'I am upset. That was my toy.' 🗣️
options: Felix is angry because his brother broke his toy 😠
Felix tells his brother, 'I am upset. That was my toy.' 🗣️
Felix's face feels hot and his hands feel very tight 🔥
quests.hint: An action is something Felix does or says.
quests.explanation: Telling his brother something is an action. A hot face and being angry are body signals and a feeling.
quests.funFact: Words are a powerful action, and they can show anger without hurting anyone.

quests.instruction: On the first day of swimming class, Lea stands at the pool edge. Which of these is a THOUGHT?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I might sink if I try' 💭
options: Lea steps back from the edge 👣
'I might sink if I try' 💭
Lea's hands shake 🤲
quests.hint: A thought is the sentence going on in your head.
quests.explanation: 'I might sink if I try' is what Lea is telling herself. Shaking hands are a body signal and stepping back is an action.
quests.funFact: Thoughts are not always true. A swimming teacher can help you test them safely.

quests.instruction: Two children feel angry after losing a game. Pia takes a deep breath and says, 'Good game.' Ned throws the ball at the wall. What is true here?
quests.correctAnswer: They both feel angry but chose different actions 🎲
options: They both feel angry but chose different actions 🎲
Pia is not really angry because she stayed so calm 🎭
Ned is angrier than Pia because he threw the ball 📈
quests.hint: Think about the difference between the feeling and the thing each child did.
quests.explanation: Feeling angry is not the same as acting angrily. Two people can feel the same and choose different actions.
quests.funFact: Taking a breath can give you a moment to choose your action instead of reacting right away.

quests.instruction: Which sentence shows that a feeling is not the same as an action?
quests.correctAnswer: I feel angry, and I can still choose calm words 🗣️
options: If I feel angry, I have to yell 📢
Angry people cannot control what they do 🚫
I feel angry, and I can still choose calm words 🗣️
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that keeps the feeling and the action separate.
quests.explanation: A feeling shows up on its own, but we have choices about what to do next. That is why calm words are possible even when we are angry.
quests.funFact: Every feeling is okay. Not every action is okay.

quests.instruction: Nikhil thinks, 'This puzzle is impossible. I will never finish it.' Which feeling is most likely?
quests.correctAnswer: Frustrated 😤
options: Excited 🤩
Calm 😇
Frustrated 😤
quests.hint: Think about what a thought like 'I will never finish' does to our mood.
quests.explanation: A thought that something is impossible tends to bring frustration. Changing the thought can change the feeling.
quests.funFact: Replacing 'I will never finish' with 'I have not finished it yet' can lift a frustrating thought.

quests.instruction: Nora feels scared before her dive. She thinks, 'I have practiced a hundred times, and my coach is right here.' Her feeling shrinks. Why?
quests.correctAnswer: Her thought gave her a reason to feel safer 🛟
options: Feelings only change when we ignore them 🙈
Her coach took away her feelings ✂️
Her thought gave her a reason to feel safer 🛟
quests.hint: Think about how a different thought can change how something feels.
quests.explanation: Thoughts and feelings are connected. A reassuring thought can make a scared feeling smaller, without pretending the feeling is not there.
quests.funFact: A helpful thought can be as simple as 'I have done this before.'

quests.instruction: After the thunder, Ishaan's heart pounds. He thinks, 'What if the roof flies off?' He feels scared and hides under a blanket. Which describes what Ishaan DOES?
quests.correctAnswer: He hides under a blanket 🛏️
options: He hides under a blanket 🛏️
His heart pounds 💓
He thinks about the roof 🏠
quests.hint: Which part could a video camera record him doing?
quests.explanation: Hiding under a blanket is a visible action. A pounding heart is a body signal, and 'What if the roof flies off?' is a thought.
quests.funFact: Telling a grown-up about a scary thought can help you test it together.

quests.instruction: Tara thinks, 'Nobody wants me here,' and stays home. Which thought could help her feel less lonely?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I can ask someone to sit with me' 💬
options: 'I will never fit in with anyone at this place' 🚪
'Nobody ever likes me or wants to sit with me' 🙁
'I can ask someone to sit with me' 💬
quests.hint: Look for a thought that leaves room for something new to happen.
quests.explanation: A thought that includes a possible action can help a lonely feeling shrink. Thoughts with 'never' or 'nobody' tend to make feelings heavier.
quests.funFact: Starting with one person, like asking a single classmate to sit with you, is a gentle first step.

quests.instruction: Kai feels jealous when his friend is picked as captain. Which action would keep their friendship safe?
quests.correctAnswer: Congratulate him and say he would like a turn next time 🤝
options: Congratulate him and say he would like a turn next time 🤝
Tell everyone in class that the captain cheated to win 📢
Hide his friend's captain cap so he cannot wear it 🧢
quests.hint: Feeling jealous is okay. Which action does not hurt anyone?
quests.explanation: Jealousy is a feeling, and congratulating the friend while asking for a turn is a respectful action. Hiding things or spreading a lie would hurt the friendship.
quests.funFact: Telling someone what you hope for next time can turn jealousy into a goal.

quests.instruction: Which one is an action, not a feeling?
quests.correctAnswer: Shouting 📢
options: Worried 😟
Disappointed 😞
Shouting 📢
quests.hint: Feelings are what we feel inside. Actions are what we do.
quests.explanation: Shouting is something a person does. Worried and disappointed are feelings.
quests.funFact: We can name a feeling quietly in our mind, but actions are what other people see.

quests.instruction: Raj thinks, 'Why does she always get picked and not me?' Choose the most likely feeling.
quests.correctAnswer: Jealous 😒
options: Calm 😇
Jealous 😒
Proud 😌
quests.hint: What does comparing yourself with someone else often bring?
quests.explanation: Comparing ourselves with someone who gets something we want tends to bring jealousy. Noticing the comparison is the first step.
quests.funFact: Focusing on your own next step can make comparing less powerful.

quests.instruction: Amir feels sad when his cousin leaves. His uncle says, 'Do not cry, be strong.' What is a better idea?
quests.correctAnswer: Feeling sad is okay, and he can choose to talk or draw about it 🎨
options: Crying means that he is weak and should be ashamed 💧
Sad feelings should always be hidden from other people 🙈
Feeling sad is okay, and he can choose to talk or draw about it 🎨
quests.hint: Think about whether a feeling is something to fight or something to understand.
quests.explanation: Sadness is a normal response to someone leaving. Talking or drawing are healthy actions that let the feeling out.
quests.funFact: Crying is a natural way for the body to release a big feeling.

quests.instruction: Dana says, 'I am so mad that I am going to ruin her project!' What can Dana still change, even though the feeling stays?
quests.correctAnswer: The action: she can choose not to ruin the project ✂️
options: The event: she can make it not have happened ⏪
The action: she can choose not to ruin the project ✂️
The feeling: she can switch off being mad 🔘
quests.hint: Which part is in her power right now?
quests.explanation: We cannot erase a feeling or undo an event, but we can choose our next action. Choosing not to ruin the project protects her and others.
quests.funFact: Taking a pause gives your brain time to find a better action.

quests.instruction: Nimmi thinks, 'If I raise my hand and I am wrong, everyone will laugh.' Which feeling is most likely?
quests.correctAnswer: Worried 😟
options: Bored 😑
Worried 😟
Proud 😌
quests.hint: What does a thought about being laughed at tend to bring?
quests.explanation: Imagining a bad outcome, like being laughed at, often brings worry. The thought makes the feeling grow.
quests.funFact: Many teachers say wrong answers help the class learn.

quests.instruction: Jae's story: 'I lost the race. I think I am too slow. I feel disappointed. I will ask the coach for tips.' What kind of part is 'I think I am too slow'?
quests.correctAnswer: A thought 💭
options: An action 🏃
A feeling 💗
A thought 💭
quests.hint: Which part is a sentence in his head?
quests.explanation: 'I think...' tells us what he believes, which is a thought. A thought is not always true.
quests.funFact: Thoughts can be checked, like asking, 'Is that always true?'

quests.instruction: Maria stomps her feet when she is angry. Is stomping the feeling, the action, or the event?
quests.correctAnswer: The action 🦶
options: The action 🦶
The event 📅
The feeling 😠
quests.hint: Think about what people can see Maria doing.
quests.explanation: Stomping is something Maria does. Anger is the feeling underneath it. The event is what caused it.
quests.funFact: If an action is not safe or kind, we can practice a different action.

quests.instruction: Gus thinks, 'It is just a game. I can try again tomorrow.' Which feeling is most likely right after this thought?
quests.correctAnswer: Calm 😇
options: Left out 🥀
Furious 😡
Calm 😇
quests.hint: Think about how a thought that puts a loss in perspective feels.
quests.explanation: A thought that puts a loss in perspective and offers another try tends to bring calm.
quests.funFact: Seeing a loss as part of learning can make it feel smaller.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the best example of choosing an action on purpose?
quests.correctAnswer: I felt scared, so I took a breath and asked for help 🙋
options: I felt scared, so I stayed silent and hoped it would pass 🤐
I felt scared, so I decided never to try again 🚫
I felt scared, so I took a breath and asked for help 🙋
quests.hint: Look for the choice that deals with the situation instead of avoiding it.
quests.explanation: Taking a breath and asking for help is a deliberate action that deals with the problem. The other choices let the scared feeling decide everything.
quests.funFact: Asking for help is a skill, and strong people use it often.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the event, not a thought or a feeling?
quests.correctAnswer: A door slammed in the hallway 🚪
options: He felt terrified 😱
A door slammed in the hallway 🚪
He thought someone was angry 💭
quests.hint: Look for the one that someone could film.
quests.explanation: A door slamming is something that happened. 'He thought' and 'He felt' describe the inside of a person.
quests.funFact: Describing the event first helps you stay calm and clear when you explain a problem.

quests.instruction: Which choice helps you check what you are feeling before you act?
quests.correctAnswer: Pause and ask, 'What am I feeling?' ⏸️
options: Act first and think later ⚡
Pause and ask, 'What am I feeling?' ⏸️
Decide that feelings do not matter 🚫
quests.hint: Which choice gives you a moment before you do something?
quests.explanation: Pausing to name a feeling gives you time to choose a helpful action. Acting first or ignoring feelings makes that harder.
quests.funFact: Naming a feeling quietly in your head can reduce how big it feels.

quests.instruction: Two children get the same grade. Lara thinks, 'I can improve with practice.' Mo thinks, 'I am just bad at this.' Whose thought is more likely to bring discouragement?
quests.correctAnswer: Mo's 😞
options: Lara's 🌱
Mo's 😞
Both are equally likely ⚖️
quests.hint: Compare how much each thought leaves room to change.
quests.explanation: 'I am just bad at this' sounds permanent, which tends to bring discouragement. 'I can improve' leaves room to grow.
quests.funFact: Adding the word 'yet,' as in 'I cannot do this yet,' can change a discouraging thought.

quests.instruction: Which action could go with sadness without hurting anyone?
quests.correctAnswer: Drawing how it feels 🎨
options: Drawing how it feels 🎨
Yelling at a friend 📢
Pretending nothing happened 🙈
quests.hint: Look for an action that lets the feeling out safely.
quests.explanation: Drawing is a safe way to let a feeling out. Yelling can hurt others, and pretending nothing happened keeps the feeling stuck inside.
quests.funFact: Many artists and writers use their work to express difficult feelings.

quests.instruction: Sandeep felt nervous before the quiz, but he still sat down and began. What does this show?
quests.correctAnswer: A feeling can be there while we choose what to do 🧭
options: Nervous people cannot do quizzes or any hard tasks 🚫
A feeling can be there while we choose what to do 🧭
He was not really nervous, because he did the quiz 🎭
quests.hint: Think about the feeling and the action as two separate things.
quests.explanation: Sandeep felt nervous and still chose to begin. Feelings can be present while we choose our actions.
quests.funFact: Starting with the easiest question can help nerves settle.

quests.instruction: Wen's story: 'The ball hit my foot. I think they will laugh. I feel embarrassed. I laughed along and picked up the ball.' Which part is the FEELING?
quests.correctAnswer: I feel embarrassed 😳
options: I think they will laugh 💭
I feel embarrassed 😳
I laughed along 😄
quests.hint: Look for the part that names an emotion.
quests.explanation: 'I feel embarrassed' names the emotion. 'I think they will laugh' is a thought, and 'I laughed along' is an action.
quests.funFact: Sorting a story into parts is a good way to understand your own reactions.

quests.instruction: Which choice separates a thought from a fact?
quests.correctAnswer: I think I failed, but I have not seen my score yet 📝
options: I think I failed, but I have not seen my score yet 📝
I failed because I am useless and always will be 🚫
Everyone in class already knows that I failed 📢
quests.hint: Which sentence is honest about what is known and what is a guess?
quests.explanation: 'I think I failed, but I have not seen my score' recognizes that it is a guess. The other sentences treat a harsh thought as a fact.
quests.funFact: A thought is a guess until we check it.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best sums up how feelings and actions work together?
quests.correctAnswer: Feelings show up on their own, and we choose what to do next 🧭
options: Feelings show up on their own, and we choose what to do next 🧭
Feelings tell us exactly what to do and when to do it 📌
Good feelings are always better than any hard ones ⭐
quests.hint: Think about who is in charge of the next action.
quests.explanation: Feelings are signals that arrive on their own. We cannot control them, but we can choose what we do.
quests.funFact: Feelings are signals. We can choose what we do next.
